lem-nonlinear-path-extension-is-a-probab:
## Statement

Let $T\ge0$ be finite, let $(\mathsf Z_t,\mathcal Z_t)$ be standard-Borel
spaces for $0\le t\le T$, and for $1\le t\le T$ let
$M_t:\mathsf Z_{t-1}\rightsquigarrow\mathsf Z_t$ be probability kernels,
with the kernel convention of
[[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]. For $1\le t\le T$, define the path-extension kernel
from $\mathsf Z_{0:t-1}$ to $\mathsf Z_{0:t}$ by
$$\overline M_t(z_{0:t-1},A)=\int_{\mathsf Z_t}\mathbf1_A(z_{0:t-1},z_t)M_t(z_{t-1},dz_t).$$
Then $\overline M_t$ is a probability kernel and $\mathsf Z_{0:t}$ is
standard Borel. Its ordered iterates append the nonlinear states with the
original transition law.
def-conditionally-linear-gaussian-state-:
## Definition

Assume AC. Let $Z_t$ take values in a standard-Borel space
$(\mathsf Z_t,\mathcal Z_t)$ and let $U_t\in\mathbb R^{d_t}$ for a finite
horizon $0\le t\le T$. For $1\le t\le T$, let
$Y_t\in\mathbb R^{p_t}$; observations begin at time $1$. The nonlinear
component has initial probability $\mu_0$ and transition probability kernels
$M_t(z_{t-1},dz_t)$; its transition does not depend on $U_{t-1}$. Given the
entire nonlinear path $z_{0:T}$, write $\mathsf Z_{0:t}=\prod_{s=0}^t\mathsf Z_s$
with its finite-product sigma-algebra and specify Borel maps
$$m_0:\mathsf Z_0\to\mathbb R^{d_0},\qquad P_0:\mathsf Z_0\to\mathbb R^{d_0\times d_0},$$
and, for $1\le t\le T$,
$$A_t:\mathsf Z_{0:t}\to\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_{t-1}},\quad Q_t:\mathsf Z_{0:t}\to\mathbb R^{d_t\times d_t},\quad C_t:\mathsf Z_{0:t}\to\mathbb R^{p_t\times d_t},\quad R_t:\mathsf Z_{0:t}\to\mathbb R^{p_t\times p_t}.$$
Require $P_0(z_0)$ and
$Q_t(z_{0:t})$ to be symmetric positive semidefinite, meaning
$v^TPv\ge0$ for every matching vector $v$, and $R_t(z_{0:t})$ to be
positive definite, meaning $v^TR_tv>0$ for every nonzero $v$. Conditional
on $Z_{0:T}=z_{0:T}$, the linear component and observations have the finite
linear-Gaussian model, with the transition and observation equations for
$1\le t\le T$:
$$U_0\sim N(m_0(z_0),P_0(z_0)),\qquad U_t=A_t(z_{0:t})U_{t-1}+\xi_t,\qquad Y_t=C_t(z_{0:t})U_t+\varepsilon_t,$$
where the centered Gaussian noises $\xi_t\sim N(0,Q_t(z_{0:t}))$ and
$\varepsilon_t\sim N(0,R_t(z_{0:t}))$ are mutually independent over time
and independent of $U_0$, under that conditional law. For every fixed path
$z_{0:T}$ these are exactly the hypotheses of
[[def-linear-gaussian-state-space-model-with-independent-noises]] with
deterministic matrices.

This hierarchical conditionally linear-Gaussian model is the input class for
the Rao–Blackwellized filter below: it samples the nonlinear path and keeps
the conditional Gaussian law of $U_t$ analytically. It does not include a
nonlinear transition whose law depends on $U_{t-1}$, nor does it assert that
the marginal nonlinear process remains Markov after conditioning on all
observations. Such models need their own marginal transition and backward
kernels. A state-space filtering or smoothing law is a data-indexed regular
conditional-distribution version as in
[[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]; no pointwise uniqueness on null data
histories is imposed.
lem-kalman-filter-is-exact-conditional-o:
## Statement

Assume the model of
[[def-conditionally-linear-gaussian-state-space-model]] and fix a nonlinear
path $z_{0:T}$. Run [[alg-kalman-filter]] on the resulting deterministic
linear-Gaussian model for a fixed observation path $y_{1:T}$. Write
$m_{t|t-1},P_{t|t-1}$ and $m_{t|t},P_{t|t}$ for its predicted and updated
moments, and define
$$v_t=y_t-C_t(z_{0:t})m_{t|t-1},\qquad S_t=C_t(z_{0:t})P_{t|t-1}C_t(z_{0:t})^T+R_t(z_{0:t}).$$
Then $\mathcal L(U_t\mid Z_{0:T}=z_{0:T},Y_{1:t}=y_{1:t})$ has the Gaussian
version $N(m_{t|t},P_{t|t})$ for every $0\le t\le T$. At time $t\ge1$, the
conditional observation density given the nonlinear path and earlier
observations is
$$\ell_t(z_{0:t};y_{1:t})=(2\pi)^{-p_t/2}\det(S_t)^{-1/2}\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12v_t^TS_t^{-1}v_t\right).$$
Each $S_t$ is positive definite, each $P_{t|t}$ is positive semidefinite,
and $\ell_t$ is finite, strictly positive, and Borel in the nonlinear path.
For every $1\le t\le T$ whose observation evidence is finite positive, the
conditional density of $Y_{1:t}$ given the nonlinear path is
$\prod_{s=1}^t\ell_s(z_{0:s};y_{1:s})$. Consequently the conditional law of
$Z_{0:t}$ given $Y_{1:t}=y_{1:t}$ is the normalized Feynman–Kac path measure
with path-extension transitions induced by $M_s$, initial potential
$G_0\equiv1$, and potentials $G_s(z_{0:s})=\ell_s(z_{0:s};y_{1:s})$. At
$t=0$ it is the initial nonlinear law $\mu_0$.
lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-fact:
## Statement

Assume AC, a finite-horizon Markov state-space model with standard-Borel
states, dominated observation kernels, and data-indexed filtering and
smoothing kernels as in
[[def-state-space-filtering-laws]]. Fix an observation history
$y_{1:T}$ in the full-measure set where the dominated filtering recursion
[[thm-dominated-state-space-filtering-recursion]] applies. Write $\eta_t$
for the filtering law of $X_t$ given $y_{1:t}$. Suppose the transition kernel
$M_{t+1}$ from time $t$ to $t+1$ has a product-measurable density
$f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)$ with respect to a sigma-finite measure $\lambda_{t+1}$,
meaning
$$M_{t+1}(x,A)=\int_A f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\lambda_{t+1}(dx')$$
for every state $x$ and measurable set $A$.
Put
$$q_{t+1}(x')=\int f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\eta_t(dx),\qquad D_{t+1}=\{x':0<q_{t+1}(x')<\infty\}.$$
The backward conditional kernel is
$$B_t(x',A)=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\int_A f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\eta_t(dx)}{q_{t+1}(x')},&x'\in D_{t+1},\\\eta_t(A),&x'\notin D_{t+1}.\end{cases}$$
It is a probability-kernel version of the conditional law of $X_t$ given
$X_{t+1}=x'$ and $y_{1:t}$. The finite-horizon smoothing kernel factors as
$$\psi_T(dx_{0:T})=\eta_T(dx_T)\prod_{t=T-1}^{0}B_t(x_{t+1},dx_t)$$
for observation-almost every full history, with the product interpreted as
successive backwards kernel integration. If the transition is supplied only
as a probability kernel, the same factorization uses a supplied regular
conditional kernel of $X_t$ given $(X_{t+1},Y_{1:t})$; no transition density
is asserted in that case. Null-history values remain version-dependent.
alg-particle-backward-simulator:
## Definition

Fix a finite horizon $T\ge0$. In the **particle mode**, the inputs are
normalized filtering clouds
$$\{(x_t^i,w_t^i):1\le i\le N\},\qquad w_t^i\ge0,\quad\sum_{i=1}^Nw_t^i=1,$$
for $0\le t\le T$, produced, for example, by
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Each $x_t^i$ is the time-$t$
coordinate of its stored particle path. Write $M_{t+1}$ for the model
transition kernel and require a product-measurable density
$f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)$ relative to a declared sigma-finite measure
$\lambda_{t+1}$, meaning
$$M_{t+1}(x,A)=\int_A f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\lambda_{t+1}(dx')$$
for each measurable $A$. For every terminal particle value used in the
backward pass, require the finite positive denominator
$$q_{t+1}^N(x')=\sum_{j=1}^Nw_t^j f_{t+1}(x'\mid x_t^j)\in(0,\infty).$$
Given a requested number $S\ge1$ of paths, repeat independently for
$s=1,\ldots,S$:

1. Draw $I_T^s$ from $\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with probabilities $w_T^i$ and set
   $\widetilde X_T^s=x_T^{I_T^s}$.
2. For $t=T-1,T-2,\ldots,0$, form
   $$b_t^i(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s)=\frac{w_t^i f_{t+1}(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s\mid x_t^i)}{\sum_{j=1}^Nw_t^j f_{t+1}(\widetilde X_{t+1}^s\mid x_t^j)},\qquad 1\le i\le N,$$
   draw $I_t^s$ from this probability vector, and set
   $\widetilde X_t^s=x_t^{I_t^s}$.
3. Return the stored particle paths indexed by
   $(I_0^s,\ldots,I_T^s)$. The output is a draw from the particle backward
   approximation to the smoothing path law. This index draw is not the same
   operation as tracing the forward filter's recorded ancestor indices.

If an exact filtering kernel $\eta_T$ and supplied backward conditional
kernels $B_t$ from
[[lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-factorization]] are available for
general transition kernels, there is a separate exact-kernel mode: draw
$X_T\sim\eta_T$ and then draw $X_t\sim B_t(X_{t+1},\cdot)$ successively
backward. This mode uses the actual kernels; it does not evaluate a
transition density or a kernel on particle singletons. It returns an exact
smoothing path under the supplied conditional versions.

An optional all-marginals mode computes particle smoothing weights instead
of drawing paths. Initialize $\bar w_{T|T}^j=w_T^j$. For
$t=T-1,\ldots,0$, set
$$\bar w_{t|T}^i=w_t^i\sum_{j=1}^N\bar w_{t+1|T}^j\frac{f_{t+1}(x_{t+1}^j\mid x_t^i)}{\sum_{\ell=1}^Nw_t^\ell f_{t+1}(x_{t+1}^j\mid x_t^\ell)}.$$
Under the same finite-positive denominator condition, normalize the computed
nonnegative values $\bar w_{t|T}^i$ to sum one and return
$\sum_i\bar w_{t|T}^i\delta_{x_t^i}$ as the approximate smoothed marginal at
time $t$. The algorithm makes no finite-particle accuracy, consistency, or
long-time stability claim.
alg-rao-blackwellized-particle-filter:
## Definition

Use the conditionally linear-Gaussian model of
[[def-conditionally-linear-gaussian-state-space-model]] and a fixed
observation path $y_{1:T}$. The particle state at time $t$ is the full
nonlinear history $z_{0:t}$; finite products of the standard-Borel state
spaces are standard Borel. Its transition appends a draw
$z_t\sim M_t(z_{t-1},\cdot)$; the resulting path-extension probability
kernel and standard-Borel path space are supplied by
[[lem-nonlinear-path-extension-is-a-probability-kernel]]. Set the initial Feynman–Kac potential to
$G_0\equiv1$ and the time-$t$ potential to the conditional observation
density
$$G_t(z_{0:t})=\ell_t(z_{0:t};y_{1:t})$$
from [[lem-kalman-filter-is-exact-conditional-on-nonlinear-path]]. Use the
same path-extension kernel as target and proposal, so the initial and
transition Radon–Nikodym weights are identically one. Run
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]] with multinomial resampling to
approximate the filtering law of the nonlinear path. Each particle stores
alongside its path the conditional Gaussian moments of $U_t$.

Initialize $N\ge1$ particles by drawing $z_0^i\sim\mu_0$ independently,
setting $w_0^i=1/N$, $m_{0|0}^i=m_0(z_0^i)$, and
$P_{0|0}^i=P_0(z_0^i)$. For each $t=1,\ldots,T$:

1. Draw ancestor indices $J_t^1,\ldots,J_t^N$ independently with
   probabilities $(w_{t-1}^1,\ldots,w_{t-1}^N)$ and append independent
   transitions $z_t^i\sim M_t(z_{t-1}^{J_t^i},\cdot)$.
2. For each particle, abbreviate its appended path by $z_{0:t}^i$ and compute
   $$m_{t|t-1}^i=A_t(z_{0:t}^i)m_{t-1|t-1}^{J_t^i},\qquad P_{t|t-1}^i=A_t(z_{0:t}^i)P_{t-1|t-1}^{J_t^i}A_t(z_{0:t}^i)^T+Q_t(z_{0:t}^i).$$
   Form $v_t^i=y_t-C_t(z_{0:t}^i)m_{t|t-1}^i$ and
   $S_t^i=C_t(z_{0:t}^i)P_{t|t-1}^iC_t(z_{0:t}^i)^T+R_t(z_{0:t}^i)$.
3. Set the incremental weight to the finite positive Gaussian density
   $$a_t^i=(2\pi)^{-p_t/2}\det(S_t^i)^{-1/2}\exp\!\left(-\tfrac12(v_t^i)^T(S_t^i)^{-1}v_t^i\right),$$
   and normalize $w_t^i=a_t^i/\sum_j a_t^j$.
4. Update the conditional Gaussian moments by
   $$K_t^i=P_{t|t-1}^iC_t(z_{0:t}^i)^T(S_t^i)^{-1},\qquad m_{t|t}^i=m_{t|t-1}^i+K_t^iv_t^i,\qquad P_{t|t}^i=P_{t|t-1}^i-K_t^iS_t^i(K_t^i)^T.$$

The procedure returns the weighted nonlinear particle paths and the Gaussian
mixture
$$\widehat\pi_t^N(du_t,dz_{0:t})=\sum_{i=1}^Nw_t^iN(du_t;m_{t|t}^i,P_{t|t}^i)\,\delta_{z_{0:t}^i}(dz_{0:t}).$$
Its conditional mean is $\sum_iw_t^im_{t|t}^i$ and its conditional covariance
is $\sum_iw_t^i[P_{t|t}^i+(m_{t|t}^i-\bar m_t)(m_{t|t}^i-\bar m_t)^T]$,
where $\bar m_t=\sum_iw_t^im_{t|t}^i$. These are moments of the finite
mixture approximation; for finite $N$ the algorithm remains an approximation
to the full nonlinear filter. It makes no general variance-reduction,
convergence-rate, or long-time accuracy claim.
lem-bootstrap-particle-filter-weak-consi:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $E_0,\ldots,E_T$ be compact metric spaces, let $\mu_0$ be a probability
on $E_0$, and let $M_t$ be a Feller probability kernel from $E_{t-1}$ to
$E_t$. Here **Feller** means that $x\mapsto M_t h(x):=\int h(x')M_t(x,dx')$
is continuous for every bounded continuous real $h$ on $E_t$. Let each
potential $G_t:E_t\to\mathbb R$ be continuous and satisfy fixed bounds
$0<c\le G_t(x)\le C<\infty$. Let $P_t^M$ be the Markov path law and
$Z_t=\int\prod_{s=0}^tG_s(x_s)\,P_t^M(dx_{0:t})$ the Feynman–Kac normalizer
from [[def-feynman-kac-path-targets-and-normalizers]]. Since $P_t^M$ is a
probability, $c^{t+1}\le Z_t\le C^{t+1}$, so the normalized path target exists.
For the initial law and transitions use the
bootstrap proposals $\nu_0=\mu_0$, $R_t=M_t$, initial potential $G_0$, and
multinomial resampling in
[[alg-sequential-importance-resampling]]. Write $\eta_t$ for the last-state
marginal of $\gamma_t/Z_t$ and
$\eta_t^N=\sum_iw_t^i\delta_{X_t^i}$ for the particle filter's current
weighted empirical measure. For every fixed $t\le T$,
$$\eta_t^N\Rightarrow\eta_t\quad\hbox{in probability as }N\to\infty,$$
where convergence in probability means that for every bounded continuous
$h:E_t\to\mathbb R$, $\int h\,d\eta_t^N\to\int h\,d\eta_t$ in probability.
This is a fixed-horizon, positive-bounded-potential result; it asserts no
time-uniform bound and no particle central limit theorem.
alg-fixed-lag-particle-smoother:
## Definition

Fix an integer lag $L\ge0$ and the normalized filtering particle clouds and
transition inputs required by
[[alg-particle-backward-simulator]]. For each time $t\in\{0,\ldots,T\}$,
put $s_t=\min(t+L,T)$. Run the particle backward simulator using only the
filtering clouds at times $0,\ldots,s_t$, draw the requested number of paths,
and retain only their time-$t$ coordinates. The resulting empirical law
approximates
$$\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:s_t}),$$
not the full smoothing law $\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:T})$ unless $s_t=T$ or
the two conditional laws happen to agree. The same procedure can use supplied
exact backward kernels when the model has no transition density; for each
$s_t$ it uses the supplied filtering kernel at $y_{1:s_t}$ and the backward
kernels for the corresponding prefix histories. On histories where these
kernels factor the truncated smoother, it samples that exact conditional law.

The procedure returns one truncated smoothing marginal per $t$. It does not
assert a bound on the lag bias, a forgetting rate, or convergence to the
full-data smoother for fixed $L$. Those conclusions require separate
conditions on the model.
thm-particle-backward-simulator-normaliz:
## Statement

Assume the finite particle-mode inputs and denominator conditions of
[[alg-particle-backward-simulator]]. The backward index probabilities at
each step are nonnegative and sum to one. In the all-marginals recursion,
the raw updated smoothing weights also sum to one, so the optional explicit
normalization in the algorithm leaves them unchanged. Count one transition
density evaluation and a bounded number of real arithmetic operations as
unit cost, and sample from a categorical vector by a linear scan of its $N$
entries. Then drawing $S$ backward paths costs $O(SN(T+1))$ operations,
including terminal draws, and computing all smoothed marginal weights costs
$O(N+N^2T)$, including initialization and output. For $T\ge1$ these are
respectively $O(SNT)$ and $O(N^2T)$; for fixed $S$, path sampling costs
$O(N(T+1))$.
thm-particle-smoothing-consistency-under:
## Statement

Assume AC and a finite-horizon state-space model with compact metric state
spaces $E_0,\ldots,E_T$, dominated observation kernels, and an observation
history
$y_{1:T}$ in the full-measure finite-positive set where
[[lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-factorization]] applies. Let $g_t(x,y)$
be the specified product-measurable observation density relative to its
sigma-finite observation measure, as in
[[thm-dominated-state-space-filtering-recursion]], and set
$G_t(x)=g_t(x,y_t)$ for $1\le t\le T$ and $G_0\equiv1$. Suppose each $G_t$
is continuous and there are constants $0<c\le1\le C<\infty$ such that
$c\le G_t(x)\le C$ for every state and time. For each $0\le t<T$, let
$M_{t+1}$ be the state transition from time $t$ to time $t+1$ and suppose it has a jointly continuous
density $f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)$ relative to a Borel probability measure
$\lambda_{t+1}$, meaning
$$M_{t+1}(x,A)=\int_A f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\,\lambda_{t+1}(dx')$$
for measurable $A$, with uniform bounds
$$0<a\le f_{t+1}(x'\mid x)\le b<\infty$$
for all $x,x'$. Write $\eta_t$ for the exact filtering-kernel value at
$y_{1:t}$ and $\psi_T$ for the exact smoothing-kernel value at $y_{1:T}$.
Use the model initial law as the initial proposal, these same
$M_t$ as transition proposals, and these $G_t$ as potentials in the
multinomial bootstrap particle filter. With $N\ge1$ particles, independently
draw $S_N\ge1$ backward paths conditional on the resulting clouds, where
$S_N\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$. Let $\widehat\psi_T^N$ be the conditional
law of one backward-simulated path given the clouds. For every continuous
$\Phi:E_0\times\cdots\times E_T\to\mathbb R$,
$$\widehat\psi_T^N(\Phi)\to\psi_T(\Phi)\quad\hbox{in probability},\qquad \frac1{S_N}\sum_{s=1}^{S_N}\Phi(\widetilde X_{0:T}^s)\to\psi_T(\Phi)\quad\hbox{in probability}.$$
For a fixed number of simulated paths, their conditional path law is
consistent but the empirical path average retains its Monte Carlo error.
No time-uniform-in-$T$ convergence claim is made.
thm-fixed-lag-smoother-targets-truncated:
## Statement

Assume AC and a finite-horizon Markov state-space model with standard-Borel
state and observation spaces. Supply the exact filtering and backward
conditional kernels of
[[lem-smoothing-backward-kernel-bayes-factorization]]. Fix an observation
history in the full-measure set on which their factorization holds for every
prefix horizon $s\le T$. In the exact-kernel mode of
[[alg-fixed-lag-particle-smoother]], fix $t$ and set
$s=\min(t+L,T)$. Each returned path's time-$t$ coordinate has conditional
law $\mathcal L(X_t\mid Y_{1:s})$ (for the supplied conditional versions),
so the empirical measure of finitely many paths is a Monte Carlo estimate of
that marginal. The target equals the full smoothing marginal only when later
observations do not change the conditional law; increasing the particle count
cannot remove a difference caused by truncating the observation history.
